name: Erupting vine
description: One stem out of a hole it made. The weapon is not a thing thrown at the ground — the ground opens and the plant is already there — so the hole is drawn first and the vine stands out of its near edge, with the soil it turned still lying where it was pushed. The hole is an ellipse at 0.38 of its width because that is the angle everything else in this game is seen at, and a round hole would read as a disc laid on top of the floor rather than as a way into it; `meta.radius` is its own width, which is the circle the weapon actually catches bodies in, so the drawing and the grab cannot drift apart. The stem is one cubic swept by a taper rather than a drawn outline, and the lit side is that same centreline pushed most of a half-width off it, which is what keeps the light on the stem however hard the stem bends. Two tendrils spring off it at a third and two thirds of its length and curl away opposite each other, so the silhouette is never symmetrical and never reads as a fork. Every outline is laid down before any fill: three plants each carrying their own ink cross each other's stems, one plant carrying it once does not. Moss for the stem, lichen for the leaves with a sage vein, and the thorns are `$husk` — bone against green, because a thorn the colour of the plant is a bump. They lean back down the stem: a barb pointing the way the stem grew is a spike, one pointing back is a hook, and this weapon holds things.

evolved.description: The same plant in the gold the arsenal's evolutions all wear. The stem darkens to gold's own ramp and the thorns take the bright end of it, while the leaves stay lichen — a vine gilded all the way through stops reading as a growing thing, and what the evolution changed is the wood, not the foliage.
